FLY LAB · BROWSER NEUROSCIENCE

How can a nervous system make a body move?

Run small experiments in a browser-local neural model, then compare them with a traced fly nerve cord. Change an input, watch spikes move through the model, and ask what the visible body does — and what it does not prove.

  • Start with one neuron
  • BANC v888 body model
  • FlyWire v783 optional
  • runs locally · no account

No movement claim is made from the walking clip. The shin responds only to measured BANC motor output or an explicitly labelled direct demo.

Controls and counterfactuals

Direct joint demo writes a rate straight to the effector and skips the neurons. It is a control, not neural evidence. Sensor silence is an explicit intervention on the current illustrative proprioceptive input.

01b — FlyWire brain model (optional 54 MB)

FlyWire v783 is a separate whole-brain model: 138,639 neurons, loaded only when you ask. Its output stays in its own panel and does not drive the walking fly.

The current build exposes aggregate spikes plus a bounded spike monitor. It does not yet export named feeding-population identities or membrane voltage.

What each model means

BANC v888: a female-CNS, leaky-integrate-and-fire nerve-cord model connected to a male procedural body through a kinematic motor-to-joint mapping.

FlyWire v783: a browser-local whole-brain simulation with its own counters and optional sugar input. Loading it does not make the visible fly walk.

Walking: a kinematic animation clip. It is a visual introduction, not an emergent connectome result.
